goal: Lets tools that generate typed bindings from Bitcoin Core's OpenRPC dump know which integer verbosity value maps to which getblock response shape.
Solves an ambiguity that forces client generators like corepc and btcd to hardcode the verbosity-to-schema mapping.
reviewability: A fresh question from maflcko about a cast is open but only just asked, not yet a blocker.
agreement: Strong support: jeanpablojp gave a concept ACK and raised several concrete gaps, all of which the author fixed (jeanpablojp).
A maintainer (maflcko) has a small open question about a cast, unresolved but very recent, not yet a stated objection.

categories.name: rpc
why: P3 because it improves the OpenRPC dump's usefulness for external client generators (corepc, btcd) but does not change any RPC's behavior, security, or compatibility.
Unblocks better auto-generated bindings for a documented but narrow class of consumers.

result.summary: This PR adds an optional RPCResultDiscriminator to the RPC help metadata, which is emitted as an OpenRPC 'x-bitcoin-discriminated-result' extension field, and applies it to getblock so that the schema documents which verbosity value selects which of the four oneOf result arms. It also documents the existing 'x-bitcoin-default-hint' extension in the getopenrpcinfo schema text and adds help text and a functional test noting that verbosity 2 and 3 responses can be schema-identical for blocks with no spent inputs. No RPC request handling or returned data changes.
result.problem: OpenRPC's dump documents getblock's four verbosity-dependent response shapes as an untagged oneOf, giving consumers that generate typed bindings per verbosity (named as corepc and btcd) no machine-readable way to know which integer picks which shape, forcing them to hardcode the mapping.

open_concerns: maflcko (2026-09-17) asked what a cast in server.cpp is for; unanswered as of the timeline but only just raised.
resolved_concerns: jeanpablojp noted the test only asserted the discriminator's literal values, not the two relations they claim (parameter name/index alignment, and which arm actually has prevout); author updated the test per the suggestion.
jeanpablojp asked whether the description should explain why validating a response can't distinguish verbosity 2 and 3; author added the explanation ('Done').
jeanpablojp suggested documenting the new extension keys in OpenRPCDocResult's help text and fixing hyphenation to match other x-bitcoin- keys; author addressed both ('Done').

jeanpablojp asked if the int-only constructor was deliberate given other oneOf discriminators use bool/string; author said yes, deliberate for this first pass, with overloads to follow in later commits when needed.

categories.name: rpc
categories.evidence: Directly modifies RPC help metadata (RPCResults, RPCResultDiscriminator), the OpenRPC dump generation in rpc/server.cpp, and getblock's RPCMethod definition in rpc/blockchain.cpp; carries the RPC/REST/ZMQ label.
categories.rationale: This is a machine-readable documentation improvement to the OpenRPC dump, not a change to any RPC's behavior or compatibility ('getblock request handling and returned block data are unchanged'). It has real but narrow value for a class of external tooling (corepc, btcd, per description) that generates typed bindings, and the PR itself notes the pattern generalizes to other multi-arm results, giving it some leverage for future documentation work, but no consumer demand is corroborated beyond the author's description.

uncertainties: Whether corepc or btcd have actually asked for this discriminator, versus the author's own framing of the use case, is not corroborated by any linked issue or external comment.
The maintainer's outstanding question about the cast could surface a real code issue once answered, which might affect reviewability if it goes unanswered past 7 days.
result.card: This PR adds an optional OpenRPC extension field, x-bitcoin-discriminated-result, that maps the getblock verbosity parameter onto its four possible result schemas, and documents that verbosity 2 and 3 can be schema-identical for blocks with no spent inputs. It changes no RPC behavior, only the machine-readable OpenRPC dump and getblock's help text, aimed at external tools like corepc and btcd that generate typed bindings per verbosity value. jeanpablojp gave a Concept ACK and found concrete gaps (a test that didn't actually pin the claimed relations, missing doc text for the new extension key), all of which the author fixed across several pushes. A maintainer (maflcko) posted a fresh, unanswered question about a cast on 2026-09-17. The PR is otherwise mergeable and Ready, with no dependencies on other open PRs.
